newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai Rayong refinery maintains 20pct crude run cut.
newsitem.headline: Thai Rayong refinery maintains 20pct crude run cut.

text.p: Rayong Refinery Co is maintaining 20-percent run cuts at its 145,000-barrel-per-day crude distillation unit (CDU) due to weak domestic demand, a source close to the company said on Thursday.
"Margins are not wonderful in Thailand for...(the refinery) to run at full capacity," the source said. Rayong has only one CDU.
The crude unit has been operating at about 80-percent, since it started up in January, due to both technical and market reasons.
The source said the refinery's output would be raised when demand in Thailand picked up.
The refinery was not set up for exports and the source said there were no plans to seek export outlets.
"The economics are lousy for export," he said.
However, the refinery exported one cargo of diesel and jet fuel during the third quarter for affiliates, he said.
Thai domestic demand is expected to pick up sometime in November after the monsoon season.
The source said Rayong has also swapped a cargo of jet fuel with Esso.
The agreement involved Esso taking a 25,000-tonne cargo of jet fuel from Rayong for export and returning a similar cargo for product inland in Thailand from its 220,000-bpd Sri Racha refinery.
The refinery is a 60-40 joint venture between Shell and the Petroleum Authority of Thailand.
